claimed.text: The Age of Disclosure, directed and produced by Dan Farah, premiered at SXSW in Austin on 9 March 2025 and reached Prime Video on 21 November 2025. It features 34 senior government, military and intelligence figures and asserts an 80-year global cover-up of non-human intelligent life.

Its on-record participants include James Clapper, Marco Rubio, Representative Andre Carson and Jay Stratton, the former director of the UAP Task Force, alongside Puthoff, Eric Davis, Travis Taylor and Garry Nolan.

Imminent, published in August 2024, debuted at number one on the New York Times list with claims of recovered non-human bodies and a decades-long secret retrieval programme. Elizondo testified that it went through DOPSR for a year and that "what is in the book is what I was told I am allowed to talk about".

The board infers that DOPSR clearance, while no endorsement of accuracy, is a Departmental decision that the book's assertions are not classified, and that the Department has never said whether they are false or true and unclassified.

His second book, Reckoning, was scheduled by HarperCollins for August 2026 with a publisher's promise of "previously undisclosed evidence" and a 20-date speaking tour; whether it went through DOPSR is not public.

Elizondo maintains he ran AATIP from about 2010, writing to Pentagon spokesperson Susan Gough in June 2020, in correspondence released under FOIA, that "The truth, as everyone involved in the program knows, is that I ran the program." He testified under oath that the government has run crash-retrieval and reverse-engineering programmes.
Unidentified premiered on History on 31 May 2019, executive produced by Tom DeLonge, and portrayed Elizondo as having led AATIP for eight years.

Bryce Zabel, showrunner of the UFO-conspiracy series Dark Skies and later chairman of the Television Academy, is credited with co-authoring A.D. (After Disclosure) with Richard Dolan. With Ross Coulthart he co-hosts Need To Know, which interviewed Elizondo in 2024; a 2023 episode note says the programme controls an unaired Grusch pre-interview, and Coulthart's NewsNation interview was where Grusch's biologics and dead pilots statements began.
UAP Gerb's The Hidden Wing alleges that Air Force legacy involvement sits in named acquisition, special-programs and security offices and names their directors as likely gatekeepers.
On the board's inference, the Department's denial turns on the word assigned, which would be technically true of duties performed collaterally or under another programme name.

contested.text: The Pentagon's line since June 2019 is that Elizondo did not lead AATIP, and a DIA memorandum reported the programme's deliverables were of limited value to the agency.
Prepublication clearance vouches for security, not truth: Grusch himself told Congress his cleared statements were his own views and opinions, not the Department's.

The videos' route to the public is disputed on paper: Elizondo's 2017 clearance form says not for publication, and the Navy stated in 2019 that neither its offices nor DOPSR had any record of a request for their unrestricted release in 2017. To The Stars published the footage on its own platform from 2017 framed as officially cleared, a framing the Navy contested.
At a May 2025 event Elizondo presented an image he described as a disc 600 to 1,000 feet across, which analysts including Mick West identified as an irrigation circle.
AARO's first director, Sean Kirkpatrick, attributed the modern crash-retrieval narrative to AATIP and Robert Bigelow's circle.
To The Stars was renamed in 2022 after Elizondo, Christopher Mellon and Justice left, and its later output is entertainment.
Zabel's co-authorship of A.D. rests on an encyclopedic source alone: neither Television Academy page mentions the book or Dolan.

lead.text: Films, series and books carry the modern UAP story to the public, and on this board they are records of what was asserted, not evidence of it. The documented part is what followed them: the History series on Luis Elizondo was followed by the Pentagon statement that he had no AATIP responsibilities, and, by Elizondo's sworn account, his book passed the Department's prepublication review.

record.text: Asked by Keith Kloor of The Intercept after the History series presented Elizondo as having led AATIP for eight years, Pentagon spokesman Christopher Sherwood said on 1 June 2019 that Elizondo had no responsibilities with regard to AATIP while at OUSD(I). On 22 May 2019 Sherwood had said AATIP did pursue research into unidentified aerial phenomena.

The Department's standing position is that Elizondo had no assigned responsibilities for AATIP, that DIA administered it and that he interacted with the DIA office but did not lead it. Susan Gough gave the same answer after the Reid memorandum was authenticated, saying it made no change to previous statements.

Elizondo testified before House Oversight on 13 November 2024 as 'Author, and Former Department of Defense Official'. His title at resignation on 4 October 2017 was Director, National Programs Special Management Staff, and his resignation correspondence was released under FOIA.

Elizondo submitted the DD Form 1910 on 9 August 2017 to clear the GoFast, Gimbal and FLIR video files, approved on 24 August 2017, with the stated purpose "Not for publication. Research and analysis ONLY".

The Defense Office of Prepublication and Security Review cleared David Grusch's two submissions for open publication on 4 and 6 April 2023, and AARO's Historical Record Report Volume I carries review number DOPSR-2024-0263.

To The Stars Academy, which DeLonge co-founded and controlled, was an SEC reporting issuer; its filings list DeLonge, Jim Semivan and Harold Puthoff as directors and Elizondo and Steve Justice as significant employees, and record about $1.09 million raised against a $50 million target, with a FY2017 net loss of $30,665,436, of which $29,535,799 was stock-based compensation.
The Department later disowned Sherwood's May 2019 acknowledgement of AATIP's UAP research as not entirely fact-based, while keeping his denial of Elizondo's role.

summary.text: The topic's artefacts are the 2025 documentary The Age of Disclosure, the History series Unidentified of 2019-2020, Elizondo's books Imminent and Reckoning, and the television work of Bryce Zabel.

Media and the institutions behind them are intertwined: Unidentified is reported as a To The Stars production executive produced by Tom DeLonge, and Elizondo was a significant employee of the company.
Media also cite each other: a 2026 UAP Gerb video on alleged Air Force structures uses The Age of Disclosure's characterisation of the Air Force as corroboration.
